In brief: A wet and humid week lies ahead for Abuja, with increasing chances of rain as the days progress, peaking at an 80% chance by the end of the week. The current conditions in Abuja are characterized by a temperature of 23°C, which feels more like 28°C due to the high humidity of 92%. This humidity is largely due to the presence of a low-pressure system in the region, which is bringing in warm, moist air from the Atlantic Ocean. As a result, residents in areas such as Maitama and Garki can expect to feel the heat more intensely, especially in the late morning and early afternoon hours. The wind is currently blowing at a gentle 4 km/h, which is not strong enough to provide significant relief from the heat.
### Monday Temperatures on Monday are expected to rise to a high of 31°C, while the low will be around 23°C. The rain chance on this day is 41%, which is relatively low compared to the rest of the week. However, my best guess is that any rainfall that does occur will be in the form of scattered thunderstorms, possibly affecting areas such as Wuse and Gwarinpa in the late afternoon. The UV index will be relatively low, around 2, due to the thick cloud cover associated with the low-pressure system. As the day wears on, the humidity will remain high, around 80%, making it feel quite muggy in the city. The wind direction on Monday will be from the southwest, blowing at around 10 km/h. This wind direction will bring in more warm, moist air from the Gulf of Guinea, contributing to the high humidity levels. Residents living in low-lying flood-prone areas should be aware of the potential for flash flooding, especially if the rainfall is intense. The good news is that the rain is not expected to be heavy, with accumulation ranges likely to be between 5-10 mm. In areas such as Aso Rock and the airport road, the temperature may feel slightly cooler due to the elevation. However, this will be offset by the high humidity, which will make it feel just as hot and uncomfortable as in the rest of the city. The traffic on the Nnamdi Azikiwe Expressway is currently light, but this may change as the day wears on, especially if there are any heavy downpours.
### Tuesday On Tuesday, the high temperature will dip slightly to 30°C, while the low will be around 22°C. The rain chance increases significantly to 65%, making it the wettest day of the week so far. Models suggest that the rainfall will be more widespread, affecting most parts of the city, including the central business district and the National Assembly (NASS) area. The wind direction will shift to the southeast, blowing at around 15 km/h, which will bring in even more moist air from the Atlantic Ocean. The humidity levels will remain high, around 85%, making it feel extremely muggy and uncomfortable. There's a chance that the rainfall could be heavy at times, with accumulation ranges likely to be between 15-25 mm. This could lead to significant traffic disruptions, especially on roads that are prone to flooding. Residents are advised to plan their journeys accordingly and to leave plenty of time to reach their destinations. The temperature in areas such as Gwarinpa and Wuse will feel particularly hot and humid, due to the urban heat island effect. This effect is exacerbated by the presence of tall buildings and paved surfaces, which absorb and retain heat. As a result, residents in these areas can expect to feel the heat more intensely, especially in the late morning and early afternoon hours.
### Wednesday On Wednesday, the high temperature will dip further to 29°C, while the low will be around 23°C. The rain chance increases again to 67%, making it another wet and humid day. The wind direction will remain from the southeast, blowing at around 10 km/h, which will continue to bring in warm, moist air from the Atlantic Ocean. The humidity levels will remain extremely high, around 90%, making it feel very uncomfortable. The rainfall on Wednesday is expected to be more intense, with accumulation ranges likely to be between 20-30 mm. This could lead to significant flooding in low-lying areas, especially if the rainfall is heavy and prolonged. Residents living in these areas should be on high alert and take necessary precautions to protect themselves and their property. The temperature in areas such as Maitama and Garki will feel slightly cooler due to the elevation, but this will be offset by the high humidity, which will make it feel just as hot and uncomfortable as in the rest of the city. The traffic on the Nnamdi Azikiwe Expressway may be affected by the heavy rainfall, especially if there are any accidents or flooding. ### Thursday On Thursday, the high temperature will dip to 28°C, while the low will be around 22°C. The wind direction will shift to the east, blowing at around 5 km/h, which will bring in slightly drier air from the Sahara Desert. However, this will not provide significant relief from the heat and humidity, as the air will still be warm and moist. The humidity levels will remain extremely high, around 90%, making it feel very uncomfortable.
